title: Dwell Time Distribution Across Splits and Clean Band
dataset_or_partition: Model splits (train, val, test); Panel 1: All stays (n=95,536); Panel 2: Clean band only (n=77,334)
variables_plotted: dwell_hours (log10), split_tag (train, val, test), train p50 (65.11h), train p85 (160.90h)
x_axis: Dwell duration in hours on log10 scale (ticks at 5, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000h)
aggregation_or_binning: 70 uniform bins in log10 space (log10(3) to log10(1500)); density normalized
investigation_purpose: Determine if dwell time forms natural multi-modal clusters and compare distributions across partitions
actual_finding: Dwell is unimodal (peak 60-70h) with heavy right tail; no natural trough exists between classes. Test split is shifted leftward (shorter dwell) due to extract truncation.
ml_implication: Target classes (ON_TIME, AT_RISK, CRITICAL_DELAY) are operational threshold choices, not natural physical modes. Boundary cases will have high label noise.
limitations: Extreme stays >1500h clipped by x-axis; does not condition on container attributes.

title: Dwell Duration Variation by Container Type, Size, and Customs Flags
variables_plotted: dwell_hours (log scale) vs CTR_TYPE (Panel 1), CTR_SIZE (Panel 2), Customs/Quarantine flags (Panel 3)
x_axis: Category levels with stay counts (CTR_TYPE, CTR_SIZE ft, Customs Flag yes/no)
y_axis: Dwell duration in hours on log scale (dotted lines = train p50/p85)
aggregation_or_binning: Grouped boxplots showing median and IQR; fliers suppressed; categories with n < 100 excluded
investigation_purpose: Measure dwell variation explained by container equipment attributes vs customs inspection flags
actual_finding: Container size and type show almost identical dwell distributions (median ~60-65h). Red-flag PIB and Behandle inspection shift median dwell dramatically to >140h. Quarantine flag alone has modest impact.
ml_implication: Static equipment features offer low univariate signal. Customs flags offer strong signal but Behandle occurs mid-stay (target leakage at arrival).
limitations: Fliers suppressed; small categories (<100 stays) excluded.

title: Extract Selection Truncation by Vessel Call Week
chart_type: 2-panel stacked time series (bar chart + log line plot)
dataset_or_partition: All labeled stays (n=95,647) across 21 weekly call cohorts
variables_plotted: Weekly stays, est_missing_pct, median_dwell_h, p85_dwell_h, clean band span
y_axis: Top: Stays per call week (count); Bottom: Dwell hours on log scale
aggregation_or_binning: Weekly call cohort aggregation (W-SUN); clean band shaded with vertical spans
investigation_purpose: Diagnose extract selection bias caused by filtering by gate-out date rather than vessel arrival
actual_finding: Extract is truncated at both edges. Early weeks (June) show high dwell because fast stays left prior to extract start. Late weeks (late September) show artificially collapsed dwell (median 25h) because slow stays had not yet departed by Sept 30. Last two weeks miss an estimated 25% and 50% of stays.
ml_implication: Test set completed stays suffer severe survivorship bias. Raw test accuracy overestimates performance by excluding slow-clearing containers.
limitations: est_missing_pct assumes clean-band dwell distribution is stationary over time.

title: Weekly Dwell Drift Versus Fixed Training Cutoffs
chart_type: 2-panel stacked time series (line plot + bar chart)
dataset_or_partition: All call weeks with stays >= 200 (n=19 weeks)
variables_plotted: Weekly p50 and p85 dwell vs fixed train p50/p85 cutoffs; % stays above train p85 (pct_critical)
y_axis: Top: Dwell hours (linear scale); Bottom: % of stays above train p85 cutoff (%)
aggregation_or_binning: Weekly call cohort aggregation; clean band shaded
investigation_purpose: Identify non-stationarity, congestion waves, and concept drift across time
actual_finding: Dataset contains one massive operational congestion wave in mid-July where weekly p85 spiked to ~260h and critical rate exceeded 28%. Operations calmed in August/September (p85 ~110h, critical rate < 8%).
ml_implication: Models trained primarily on July data experience prior probability shift when tested on late August/September. Static decision thresholds will over-predict critical delay.
limitations: Right edge (late September) is confounded by right-truncation.

title: Daily Vessel Call Rhythms and Weekly Schedule Gaps
chart_type: 2-panel chart (daily time series + weekday bar chart)
dataset_or_partition: Daily call date aggregates in dense operational window (104 unique call dates)
variables_plotted: Daily stays, zero-call days with weekday callout, weekday mean stays, zero-call count
x_axis: Left: Calendar date; Right: Day of week (Mon-Sun)
aggregation_or_binning: Daily volume count; weekday mean within clean band
investigation_purpose: Determine if calendar gaps represent data loss or operational shipping rhythm
actual_finding: 9 calendar dates have zero vessel calls; 8 of the 9 are Thursdays. Thursday averages only 332 stays/day vs 850-1200 on other days, and 7 of 11 Thursdays had zero calls. This is a liner schedule pattern, not missing telemetry.
ml_implication: Explains regular weekly volume drops. Continuous calendar reindexing in rolling metrics is essential so missing Thursdays do not break time-window continuity.
limitations: Specific to this terminal liner service schedules.

title: Operational Noise Floor of the 7-Day Delayed Share
chart_type: 2-panel time series (delayed share with noise envelope + departure volume bars)
dataset_or_partition: Stays indexed by gate-out date (truck_out_end_ts, n=95,647)
variables_plotted: Trailing 7d delayed share (%), 21d centered median level, +/- 2-sigma noise envelope, daily departure volume
y_axis: Top: % stays AT_RISK or CRITICAL; Bottom: Completed departures per day
aggregation_or_binning: Daily gate-out aggregates, 7-day trailing rolling proportion, 21-day centered median
investigation_purpose: Measure natural operational variance in historical delay rate and calculate minimum detectable shift
actual_finding: Trailing 7-day delay share moves by +/- 2.7 pp (1-sigma) due to daily operational randomness, 4.9x larger than binomial sampling noise. Delay rate shifts smaller than 5.4 pp (2-sigma) cannot be distinguished from noise.
ml_implication: Establishes baseline noise floor. Modeling pipelines should not try to fit sub-5% daily noise in historical delay metrics. Alert thresholds must clear 5.4 pp.
limitations: 21-day centered median is a retrospective analysis tool (requires lookahead) not usable as real-time feature.

title: Weekly Reporting Coverage of Optional Container Milestones
dataset_or_partition: Clean-band call weeks (n=10 weeks) across optional event types
variables_plotted: Activity coverage share (%) per call week for activities with < 99.5% mean coverage
investigation_purpose: Detect telemetry reporting drift, milestone drop-off, or administrative logging changes
actual_finding: Core activities have 100% coverage. Optional activities drift significantly over time: quarantine flags range from 18% to 38% across weeks; red-flag PIB ranges from 3% to 8%. Coverage variance exceeds binomial noise by up to 10x.
ml_implication: Features derived from optional milestones are non-stationary inputs. Models relying on fixed weights for quarantine flags will experience concept drift.
limitations: Cannot distinguish whether unrecorded events did not happen or were unlogged.

title: Covariate and Target Label Shift Across Partitions
chart_type: 2-panel chart (horizontal PSI bar chart on symlog + stacked class mix bar chart)
variables_plotted: Left: PSI for val vs train and test vs train across 20 features; Right: Target class mix (% ON_TIME, AT_RISK, CRITICAL_DELAY)
x_axis: Left: Population Stability Index (symlog scale, dashed at 0.1 and 0.25); Right: Split name
y_axis: Left: Feature name; Right: % of stays (0-100%)
aggregation_or_binning: PSI binned by train deciles; label mix stacked to 100%
investigation_purpose: Measure covariate shift and target label drift between training, validation, and test
actual_finding: Static equipment features (CTR_SIZE, carrier_prefix) have near-zero PSI (< 0.05). Rolling features have massive PSI (> 3.0) due to abatement of July congestion. Target class critical delay falls from 15.0% in train to 7.4% in val and 2.8% in test.
ml_implication: Severe label and covariate shift. Models trained with fixed class weights will over-predict critical delay on validation and test.
limitations: Test split PSI is distorted by right-truncation.

title: Milestone Timing Distribution Relative to Container Discharge
dataset_or_partition: All cleaned events across all stays (n=952,069 events)
variables_plotted: Offset in hours from DISCHARGE start (t0=0): p10, median, p90; color indicates pre-discharge (blue) vs in-yard (orange)
x_axis: Hours relative to DISCHARGE start (negative = pre-discharge, positive = post-discharge)
y_axis: Activity name annotated with % occurring before discharge
aggregation_or_binning: Empirical quantiles (p10, p50, p90) per activity
investigation_purpose: Ground-truth empirical audit of operational feature availability and target leakage
actual_finding: BAPLIE occurs median 29.3h before discharge (99.99% pre). VESSEL_ATB occurs median 5.5h before discharge (100% pre). JOB_DEL occurs median 32.2h AFTER discharge. Quarantine and PIB flags are split (32.6% and 45.6% occur after discharge). BEHANDLE inspections occur 100% in-yard.
ml_implication: Irrefutable proof of target leakage. JOB_DEL_DOCTYPE, total_events_in_stay, and has_behandle_inspection must be masked at arrival. Quarantine/PIB flags cannot be used without arrival-time filtering.
limitations: Date-only midnight timestamps (00:00:00) for customs events distort sub-day hourly offsets.

title: Diurnal and Day-of-Week Operational Discharge Cycles
variables_plotted: Panel 1: Stays by discharge weekday x hour; Panel 2: Median dwell hours for cells with >= 30 stays
aggregation_or_binning: 2D binning (7 weekdays x 24 hours = 168 cells); cells with < 30 stays masked in dwell panel
investigation_purpose: Detect operational shift rhythms, staffing bottlenecks, and cyclical dwell patterns
actual_finding: Discharge operates 24/7 continuously. Containers discharged on Fridays and Saturdays dwell substantially longer (median 75-85h) than those discharged on Tuesdays and Wednesdays (median 55-60h), reflecting weekend customs closures and consignee trucking delays.
ml_implication: Validates discharge_hour, discharge_day_of_week, and is_weekend as safe, non-leaking predictors available at arrival time.
limitations: Does not control for liner service cargo mix differences across weekdays.
